set.layering_notes: Unincorporated-county-only money (fee is charged only on unincorporated residential permits). Normally paired with 4% credits plus bonds or 9% credits, SHRA HOME, PLHA and the County Housing Trust Fund in one SHRA award. Developer side of the ordinance: market-rate projects may instead dedicate land, build units, enter a development agreement with an Affordable Housing Strategy, or buy banked unit credits from SHRA; multifamily projects with at least 20% affordable units at 17 or more units per acre are exempt from the fee, which is itself a meaningful incentive for mixed-income rental. AHO is a local below-market loan, so the Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption may apply if no HOME or CDBG is in the stack; confirm with counsel. The County is mid-way through an AHO amendment study (Housing Element Program E3): KMA found 2% to 14% affordable production versus the 10% target; Board workshop Oct 6, 2026, nexus study through spring 2027, ordinance hearings expected winter 2027, possibly adding an inclusionary option and resource-area targeting. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: False for the JPA conduit bond issuance itself: DIR Public Works Case No. 2006-001, Horizons at Indio (March 12, 2007), https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf, following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village, held that publicly offered multifamily housing revenue bonds issued by a conduit issuer (CSCDA), with proceeds and repayments assigned to a private trustee, are not a payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4); even if they were, the affordable housing loan exemption (40% of units at or below 80% AMI for 20 years, 1720(c)(5)(E), formerly (c)(6)(E)) would apply. The County staff report for item 26-255 states CMFA debts are not obligations of the County, and the County only holds the TEFRA hearing. Applies to the bond issuance only; County AHF, HOME, CDBG, HACSM vouchers or other public money in the same deal is analyzed separately and can trigger state prevailing wage or Davis-Bacon.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule: the 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage provision, and the County's PLHA amendment staff report and Resolution 26-317 certifications (https://legistar.granicus.com/nevco/attachments/7d500d37-79a8-450c-820d-b92b30542adf.pdf) are silent. Coverage of a County PLHA loan is a general Labor Code 1720(b) question that turns on 1720(c) exemptions, including the 1720(c)(5)(E) affordable housing exemption (numbered (c)(6)(E) when DIR PW 2006-020 applied it), and on any HOME or CDBG layered in the trust fund loan.
